ruling.recommended_action: Close the case with no fare adjustment; record on the trip file that the driver's reroute was covered by the rider's prior consent, and note that band-2 congestion alone did not independently exempt the segment.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a fixed-quote RydeX ride: $30.99 was quoted and billed at base $3.90 + distance $19.67 (13.95 km) + time $5.95 (22.9 min) + waiting $0.00 + platform $1.47 [F6], and the billed distance of 14.0 km does not exceed the optimal 14.0 km [F4]. Under RD-2's non-metered branch, detour mileage does not enter a fixed fare (any rebate would be limited to ERP/tolls or unpublished post-trip add-ons), so even if the single off-route segment counts, the recoverable amount is zero [F4][F6][RD-2]. The rate arithmetic is not applicable here: distance fare $19.67 ÷ 13.95 km = $1.4100/km, but the 4.08 km of extra driving [F3] was never billed, so 4.08 km × $1.4100/km = $5.75 is not a charge the rider paid and cannot be refunded on a fixed-quote trip [F3][F6][RD-2].

One off-route segment exists: 22:33–22:42, 5.74 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.66 km, +4.08 km and up to 1450 m off route, on a trip that ran 18.5 km against a 14.0 km optimal route (+33%) [F1][F3], so the RD-1 shortest-and-most-direct duty is engaged [RD-1].

The driver's traffic justification cannot independently exempt that segment: the only speed-band fact is Central Expressway band 2 (10–19 km/h) during 22:06–22:33 [F11], and band evidence is corroborative only under RD-4(b) (a single band does not exempt), while no traffic incident near the route is recorded [F14], so RD-4(a) fails and the segment falls through to RD-2 [F11][F14][RD-4].

The decisive question is the scope of the rider's consent. The driver asked at 22:29 "Jam on Central Expressway is building up ahead, can I go round via Lower Delta Road?" [F7] and the rider answered at 22:29 "Sure, go ahead." [F8]; the chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F9], so the rider's own message precedes the 22:33 segment start [F3][F8][RD-5]. That message expressly assents to the driver's proposed reroute via Lower Delta Road, i.e. it is assent to the driver's chosen alternative route rather than a bare "whichever way is faster" general authorisation, and it is not an errand or stop of the driver's own — the record shows no stop or loop reaching nothing [F8][RD-5]. On the record read as a whole I read the scope as covering the reroute the driver proposed and then drove, so the segment is exempt and no unexempted deviation remains [F8][F10][RD-5]. The driver's post-trip statement alone could not supply consent, and I do not rest on it [F10][RD-5]; the record does, however, place the segment on the consented road, since the only reroute ever discussed was the one driven and no fact places the car elsewhere [F7][F8][F3].

Since there is no unexempted deviation and the fare is a fixed quote with only published components — base, distance, time, $0.00 waiting and the published $1.47 platform fee — nothing is refundable under RD-2 or FARE-1 [F4][F6][FARE-1]. RD-6 does not apply because the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the 90-day window [F17][RD-6], so there is no account flag.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement; nothing is a threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation — the complaint is only that the way round was longer [F7][F8][F10]. Safety concern: none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

All system records (gps, fare, complete timestamped chat) are present and consistent, so the record settles every element this ruling needs; account profile facts [F16][F17] did not decide anything [RD-6].

The assent was to the driver's own proposal to go round via Lower Delta Road to reach the same destination, not to an errand or stop of the driver's own, and no fact places the driven segment anywhere other than the consented reroute, so the segment is covered by the rider's consent [RD-5]. [F8][F9] covers the driver's proposed reroute (RD-5), so it does not generate a refundable deviation [RD-1][RD-5].

Rejected: reading the words, F8 is assent to the driver's specifically stated reroute 'go round via Lower Delta Road' [F7][F8], not a bare general assent, and the record ties the segment to that reroute — the only alternative ever discussed — with nothing placing the car elsewhere; the needed tie-in record exists [F7][F8][F9] so G13's undetermined outcome does not arise [RD-5].

Accepted and not in dispute: the driver's post-trip statement [F10] cannot itself supply consent [RD-5], and the ruling does not rely on it — consent rests solely on the rider's timestamped message [F8][F9].

Accepted: band 2 on Central Expressway during 22:06–22:33 [F11] is corroborative only and no incident is recorded [F14], so RD-4(a) is unmet and the driving time (not the mileage) falls to RD-2 [RD-4][RD-2]. This does not revive refund in this case because the segment is exempt under RD-5 and the fare is fixed [F4][F6][RD-5].

Accepted on the amount: the billed distance 14.0 km does not exceed the optimal 14.0 km [F4] and the RydeX fare is a fixed quote [F6], so the detour mileage was never charged and the refundable amount is zero under RD-2's non-metered branch [RD-2]. Its request for a recorded RD-1 violation is modified: the segment is exempt under RD-5, so no unexempted deviation is recorded [RD-1][RD-5].
Accepted: the fare breakdown holds only published components (base, distance, time, $0.00 waiting, published $1.47 platform fee), so FARE-1 yields no refund item [F6][FARE-1].
Accepted: the driver has 0 upheld route disputes in the 90-day window [F17], so RD-6's precondition for flag_account is not met and no account flag attaches [RD-6].

Accepted as my own screening finding: nothing in the chat, statement or complaint is a threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10], so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 do not apply [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Rejected: the advocate's own narrowed version is the correct one — no fact ties the segment to the name 'Lower Delta Road' by road name [F3], so the scope is not read as a named-road match; the ground is instead general consent to the driver's proposed reroute [F7][F8][RD-5].

Rejected as an exemption ground: band 2 at 22:06–22:33 [F11] with no incident [F14] cannot exempt the segment under RD-4(b), which requires incident evidence under RD-4(a) or corroboration only; the exemption rests on the rider's prior consent [F7][F8][RD-4][RD-5].

Not adopted as a ruling basis: the +8.2 min over estimate [F2] is not separately chargeable on a fixed-quote trip and does not affect the amount; the time component billed was 22.9 min [F6][RD-2][FARE-1].
